Hisost Yamok (希索斯特亚莫克, S23)

Region (English scoring-table region): Sarhal.

One-line identity: Lead humans, gnolls, and rhino riders in revenge for an assassinated king, then force the victors to face the slaves they created.

Story: Very high | Mission-tree length: Long (39 directly defined S23 missions) | Mission-tree update: local mission file modified in July 2026, supports v1.37.5.0 | Uniqueness: Very high | How boxed-in it feels: High | Early pressure: High | Expansion: Very high

The kingdom north of the river

The Chinese localization renders Hisost Yamok (S23) as 希索斯特亚莫克. It already exists in 1444 as a Mengi kingdom north of the Keygas River, rather than a formable nation waiting for the player; the current base Mod gives it its own country history and 39 S23-specific missions, and no successor Tag required by the main mission line has been verified. It begins as a monarchy, with Ofehibi as its primary culture and Fieldstalker Gnolls as an accepted culture; the kingdom follows Sky Domain, but its military and political life has never been a single-people affair.

The base Mod's national-idea text traces the founding to 1309: the disgraced prince Sanzon from Matamot crossed the Keygas, conquered the four surviving kingdoms on the western bank over five years, and established Hisost Yamok on the frontier. He and his successors encouraged immigration, gradually turning the difficult savanna into the kingdom's heartland. This is the idea text's account of the country's prehistory; later wars and expansion are also written into the same idea group and must not be poured wholesale into the 1444 starting map.

The ideas also say that Raheni colonizers assassinated the king in 1442, hoping to collapse the kingdom, but instead rallied its people around his young daughter Seble. The opening history script lists her as heir in 1443 and sets a regency in power. She is both the focus of the country's legitimacy and the engine of the revenge missions. The 2025 official development diary places the death of her father, the queen's campaigns, and the later political turn in one mission story; the currently playable content remains governed by the local scripts.

Seble's war and legacy

The first act must stabilise the child-ruled kingdom, then attack the Raheni colonial outposts on the northern coast. Seble can personally lead armies and advance missions during her lifetime, accumulating legacy points; after her death, the country enters a new political situation. This gives the early conquest time pressure, but it does not mean every mission has one fixed completion deadline. Victory on the coast is a player objective; the idea text's account of the queen's adult achievements is setting history and does not guarantee that every save will reproduce it.

The army's signature forces are Awirenya Rhino Riders and Rabwag Gnoll infantry. The idea text says that Seble formally incorporated the kingdom's gnolls into the army in her youth, creating lightly armoured infantry able to keep pace with rhino charges; the opening setup also genuinely accepts Fieldstalker Gnolls. Religiously, the Mengi chiefly worship Amilak, while long coexistence with the gnolls on the frontier leaves Kvangahga traditions present. The missions push these identities toward military integration, Sky Domain conversion, and cross-regional conquest, rather than treating gnolls as merely replaceable mercenaries.

Three layers of play pull against one another. First, the cavalry and the queen's personal story encourage quick battlefield results. Second, the gnolls' status and military role become political questions in the struggle over noble power. Finally, after conquering the Raheni, the missions give the player a revenge narrative against the old colonisers while forcing the state to govern the people and land it has acquired. The player can pursue very strong military performance; a 2025 GitLab test-build post and a later full-campaign review both mention cavalry strength, but their exact bonuses and routes are period-specific personal experience, not fixed current-version values.

The victors must also stand trial

The early mission text is deliberately sharp: crimes committed by Raheni rulers are expanded into collective guilt for ordinary Raheni people, and the conquerors are to make them atone through labour. At the same time, Ofehibi society itself profited from the slave trade for a long time. The colonial harm cannot turn either practice into righteous compensation. The later story puts the kingdom through an aristocratic coup after Seble; gnolls are persecuted and lose property and family, and the country must repair the damage done to them. The mission text also explicitly recognises that enslaved civilians did not choose the crimes of their rulers and that collective labour is not legitimate.

Thus “atonement” is more than dialogue. S23_restitution requires construction in former penal-labour areas, changes some provinces' lasting penalties, and grants new industries; S23_our_own_sins requires buildings and development in the country's slave-producing provinces, grants an abolition modifier, and uses random effects to convert at most 22 slave-good provinces into cloth, paper, iron, cotton, or grain. The mission narrative declares nationwide abolition, but the script does not iterate through and remove every remaining slave-producing province; if a save contains more than the convertible amount, the trade good cannot be claimed to have disappeared everywhere. This scope difference requires in-game or further script verification.

The later half still contains conversion, steppe warfare, and territorial objectives toward the Raheni. It is not a story of abandoning power after atonement; it asks a still-expanding kingdom to stop treating other people as property for collective penance. Two official diaries record the 2023 cross-species military-political design and the 2025 mission-tree preview; they explain the creative context but do not replace the current base Mod. The bounded offline query returned no dedicated Hisost Yamok country main page, while returning a regional country list and a local cheese entry; these related results cannot independently fill in the detailed national history. The Halann historical map helped locate the idea text, but its intermediate dates and province-by-province boundaries are not used as this article's official history.

Personality, values, and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 93/100 | Autocracy 72/100 | Magic↔Artifice 50/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 12/100) | Pluralism 72/100. The personality changes by phase: Seble's revenge and collective labour (Autocracy 83, Pluralism 48) → post-coup repair and atonement (Autocracy 61, Pluralism 77). The campaign is built on cross-regional conquest; monarchy and regency are pronounced, while human–gnoll co-rule and later repair raise pluralism. The early revenge phase is Autocracy 83, Pluralism 48 and the later repair phase is 61, 77; strong faith does not mean that the gameplay is centred on spellcasting or artificery.

The v2.1 values are Neutral (65/100), with a redemption trajectory. The phases are revenge and collective labour (Evil 25/100) → reparations, repair, and abolition route (Good 84/100). The phase scores are Evil 25 early and Good 84 later: collective enslavement and the existing slave trade directly violate personhood, while later rejection of collective guilt, reparations for gnoll victims, and abolition are substantive repair. War, conquest, monarchy, and conversion were not used to add or subtract value points by themselves. The overall score retains the weight of the early conduct; a later slogan does not automatically cancel it.

This is suited to players who want large-scale cavalry conquest, a queen's life and posthumous politics, a multi-species army, and a moral turn. If you only want to snowball quickly and do not want to handle succession crises, religious integration, or construction in former slave-producing provinces, this long route will be punishing. Detailed sources, version boundaries, and unresolved points are on the evidence page.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and scripted effects. Traditions apply when this idea group is adopted, the seven ideas unlock in order as the group is invested in, and the ambition applies after all seven ideas are unlocked. Only the national ideas themselves are listed; racial, governmental, and mission rewards are not mixed into the values. A new idea set after formation is not automatically added on top of the old one. Idea descriptions may recall history or describe a future ideal; they do not automatically mean that the content has already happened in 1444.

Hisost Yamok (S23) — Hisost Yamok Ideas

Tradition: Hisost Yamok Traditions

Effect: Domestic trade power: +10%; Cavalry combat ability: +15%.

Idea 1: Born From Little

The Keygas River forms the northern border of Amilak’s domain, beyond which lie savannas and deserts full of roaming gnollish packs, no civilization to be found. Yet, many Mengi sought to expand into this hostile, empty land. They built settlements on the west bank, initially as trading posts with the gnolls. Over time, these settlements grew into proper cities in their own right, even as they came increasingly under attack by the wild barbarians. Yet by the 1300s, all but four of these kingdoms were gone, hugging the great bend of the Keygas between Matamot and Dakmender.

In 1309, a disgraced prince from Matamot named Sanzon crossed the Keygas with an army of mercenaries, seeking to build a kingdom of his own. Over the course of 5 years, he conquered the four remnant kingdoms of the left bank, founding the kingdom of Hisost Yamok. Sanzon would go on to reign for another 33 years, pushing inland and decreeing a series of laws that incited a wave of immigration to his land. His successors would continue his immigrant friendly policies, helping to develop the seemingly untameable savanna.

Effect: Construction cost: -10%.

Idea 2: Seble, The Indomitable Queen

In 1442, Raheni colonizers, looking to expand their reach further up the river Keygas, assassinated the king of Hisost Yamok. The kingdom was left with only his 9 year-old daughter, Seble, available to take the throne. The plan was that his death would throw the nation into chaos, but this goal was so nakedly obvious to the people of Hisost Yamok that it backfired. The country rallied around Seble and swore revenge on the Raheni colonizers for their vain attempts to tear the country apart.

Seble herself grew up to be a particularly ferocious foe to the Raheni, and a constant thorn in their side for her entire life. Fueled by revenge, she led an invasion force at the age of 18 into Madriamilak's northern coast. In a string of remarkable victories, she laid siege to the outposts of Prukakhin and Davharral, eventually forcing them to flee the colonies.

Effect: Morale damage: +10%.

Idea 3: Divine Diarchy

The northern border of the holy lands of Madriamilak is very clear: Everywhere north of the Keygas River was not part of Amilak’s domain. This led the people of Hisost Yamok to have a slightly different relationship with their faith than other Mengi. You and your neighbors lived beyond the frontier in lands not blessed by Amilak and had to band together and use every resource you could find to survive and stay true to your beliefs.

These beliefs were influenced heavily by the large fieldstalker gnoll population that lived in the region. Unlike their brethren elsewhere in Sarhal and Bulwar, most fieldstalker gnolls never adopted demon-worship and instead followed Kvangahga, a faith that also valued resourcefulness and interdependence. Although the humans still primarily worship Amilak, it’s not uncommon to find tools branded with the symbol of Kvanga as a nod to the two gods, seen as working in tandem with each other.

Effect: Tolerance of the true faith: +2.

Idea 4: Awirenya

Since ancient times our people have seen rhinos as sacred animals, worthy of respect due to their strength and indomitable spirit. Killing one is seen as great sacrilege and punished by death. Only those born of noble blood are worthy enough to become Awirenya, the Rhino Riders.

They see their rhinos as friends and companions, both when riding through savanna and when charging into battle. To be an Awirenya is to obtain great prestige, as even among royalty only those who are chosen by the animal themself to create a bond of rider and mount can win this title. Those who are rejected are often wounded or even trampled to death.

Traditional Awirenya charges were simple yet effective. However as warfare changed, so did the tactics. In the era of gunpowder it became popular to put steel armor on the rhino, to help its skin repel bullets more effectively.

Effect: Cavalry shock: +25%.

Idea 5: The Rabwag

Before she came of age, Seble had been fed story after story of the Raheni’s decrepit actions and told that she must lead the Ofehibi people in the name of revenge. This much she absorbed and saw as her duty to perform, but where she differed from her advisors was that this should be the sole duty of the Ofehibi. She had been taken on many expeditions to meet with gnoll traders to secure weapons for her army as a teenager, and was impressed by the guards that traveled with the gnoll caravans, who towered over her own royal guards once they dismounted their rhinos.

At the age of 16, in her first decree dictated solely by herself and not the regency council, she announced that the many gnolls living in Hisost Yamok would be integrated into the military. These would be known as the Rabwag; a lightly armored infantry unit that moved in a loose formation, able to keep up with the pace of the rhino cavalry. The increased speed of these forces is a large part of why Seble was able to out-maneuver the Raheni forces in the capture of the northern coast of Madriamilak.

Effect: Movement speed: +15%.

Idea 6: The Sarkamipi Struggle

While historically the people of Hisost Yamok had enjoyed a cordial relationship with the fieldstalker gnolls that lived to the north, that started to change as the gnolls organized into a singular state. This new rising power, Haraagtseda, quickly became an existential issue when their expansionist intent grew more clear.

In 1481, Haraagtseda invaded and laid siege to the capital city. Reinforcements were able to break the siege before the situation grew too dire, but the event prompted the then 48-year-old queen to start reinforcing the northern border. The homeland of Hisost Yamok wasn’t blessed with naturally defensible terrain, so the fortifications were built out of earthwork with large moats dug around them and a short stone wall on the other side. These Grass Forts, as they were known, were quick to construct and significantly more effective than their simplistic structure would lead one to believe.

Effect: Fort maintenance: -15%.

Idea 7: A Gnollish Mengi King

The border with Haraagtseda continued to be a dangerous place for very many years, long after Queen Seble passed away. The growing tension extended to the gnoll population who lived in Hisost Yamok, with voices growing larger each year that they couldn’t trust the military if it was staffed with gnolls. Seble’s great-grandson, King Imra, made it his task to reform the army and ensure no gnolls could hold a position higher than a basic foot soldier. Any gnoll who tried to give orders would be court-martialed and possibly executed.

Within a week of passing the decree, a coup d'etat was staged against Imra and he was beheaded by one of his gnoll generals, who assumed the throne. This threatened to break out into a full civil war, but the new gnollish royal family had the full support of the Awirenya. Generations of rhino cavalry riders had fought side-by-side with their gnollish comrades. To demote gnolls to second-class citizens was seen by them as treason against the state itself. Any human or gnoll who tried to break this historic bond was not seen as worthy of leading their country.

Effect: Number of promoted cultures: +2.

Ambition: Hisost Yamok Ambitions

Effect: Number of diplomats: +1.
